title: Regulatory Capital
description: Run pyvar's 30 regulatory-capital functions on the live pyvar.com API: Basel III/IV ratios and output floor, ICAAP/SREP Pillar 2, FRTB, MiFID II, EMIR/SFTR, AIFMD/UCITS/Solvency II and CRR2 buffers. Use when the user wants a capital ratio, buffer or regulatory test computed rather than only explained. Needs a free pyvar API key; the skill explains how to get one.
tagline: Regulatory calculations: capital ratios and buffers, Pillar 2, FRTB, MiFID II, EMIR, fund regulations. The thresholds are the published Basel/EU values and are fixed, not parameters. Pick the function in **Functions** below.

examples.title: CET1 ratio, combined buffer and leverage ratio for one bank
examples.intro: Three independent calls on the same balance sheet (any one currency unit). Each returns the ratio and whether it meets the regulatory minimum.

examples.title: Basel IV output floor
examples.intro: Internal-model RWA cannot fall below 72.5% of the standardised RWA. Here the floor binds.

notes.basel_iii_cet1_ratio: Basel III Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio; minimum 4.5% (Basel III §50)
notes.basel_iii_tier1_ratio: Basel III Tier 1 Capital Ratio; minimum 6.0% (Basel III §50)
notes.frtb_pl_attribution_test: Spearman rank correlation + variance ratio, jointly evaluated (CLAUDE.md §4.4 / BCBS d457)
notes.mifid_ii_best_execution_metric: quantity-weighted price improvement vs. a reference price, in bps. NOT an RTS 27/28 figure: RTS 27 (DR (EU) 2017/575) and RTS 28 (DR (EU) 2017/576) define different fields (simple/volume-weighted prices & spreads; execution-venue rankings), not this metric, and RTS 27 was repealed by the 2024 MiFIR review. A prior docstring cited "RTS 27/28" directly for this function; corrected in the citation cleanup pass (see "Citation cleanup" below). Useful internal TCA metric, just not a regulator-prescribed one.
notes.emir_clearing_obligation_check: EMIR REFIT (Reg. (EU) 2019/834) Art. 4a(1) / Art. 10(1). Takes `notionals: dict[str, float]` (gross notional per asset class the counterparty holds — NOT a single asset_class/notional pair) plus counterparty_category ("FC"/"NFC+"/ "NFC-") and clearing_thresholds. For an FC, breaching the threshold in ANY ONE asset class puts ALL of that counterparty's asset classes in scope (Art. 4a(1)) — this is why `notionals` must cover every class, not just the one being queried. For an NFC+, each asset class is evaluated independently (Art. 10(1)); NFC- is always exempt. Returns clearing_required as a dict keyed by asset class, plus an any_class_breached flag. See "EMIR clearing scope" below.
notes.solvency_ii_scr_credit_risk: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 200(1)-(3). Capital is a TIERED multiplier on sigma (the loss std. dev.), not a flat 3x: 3*sigma while sigma/total_LGD <= 7%; 5*sigma while 7%-20%; capped at total_LGD above 20%. No risk_factor parameter — the tiers are fixed by the Delegated Regulation. [LIMITATION] the variance computed is the intra-counterparty term only (independent-Bernoulli); Art. 201's inter-counterparty correlation term (V_inter) is not computed, so the true SCR is at least as large as what this returns — see "Solvency II SCR credit-risk fix" below.
